title: Re-Writing All My Games...
author: RegularJournalist720
selftext:
Hello!

I've been writing games for a long time.  I had big dreams at first, but as a solo dev I realized that, as hard as I try, I'm never going to be able to spend the time (or have enough energy), to make a really polished game.  So I stopped... for a long time.

Then AI showed up.  I decided to revisit all those old games and see what *we* can do.

One of the biggest problems has always been dealing with big fat assets.  If you want to make a web game (my platform of choice) you can't ask the user to sit there and download megabytes of stuff.  Well you can but they probably won't be there when it's done.

I have been focusing on graphic packages like Skia, Three.js, Phaser, Pixi.js and so on.  For sound I have been working on custom tooling using tone.js.

For me it's been a slow process.  One of your jobs as an AI programmer is to be able to communicate.  Through the use of custom tooling, not only can you create your assets, but add as much tutorial/hand holding as you need.  For example I knew almost nothing about digital sound processing, but creating tools that teach is a big help.

In my experience, nothing about AI dev is a 'one prompt' solution.  If you want to write Tetris/Pac-man/Flappy Bird then you'll be ok.  If you want to do anything even close to original/unique then AI is going to struggle, and you're basically on your own.

When you start pushing the envelope on what AI has seen and done many times before, it starts staring into the abyss, and can come up with some pretty janky sh!t.

To that extent, I spend most of my time building tools: level editors, sound boards, material/texture tuners, NPC planners, etc.

When I first started posting content I got some typical "more AI Slop" comments, which I found discouraging, and so I am happy to find this community.  

In my mind I worked just as hard to build this AI game as I would have without it.  I just got more done, and could accomplish things I could never do on my own.

So far I have finished one game on the list.  This is a Spin-Art / Spirograph simulation that I wrote 5 or 6 years ago using paper.js.  The new version is a web-app using Skia graphics (check out Demo Mode!).

Old version: [https://budgesoft.com/whirlart/](https://budgesoft.com/whirlart/)

New version [http://budgesoft.com/spindoodly/](http://budgesoft.com/spindoodly/)

I look forward to posting more content

BudgeSoft

comments.author: Zestyclose_Day4993
comments.body:
That's right. Creating games with AI isn't a single prompt. I was exactly like you and I started to create games thanks to AI. So good luck my friend. 

Ignore all these AI slop comments. Some no-AI games can be slop too and some AI games can be a masterpiece. The real difference is made by the developer. If you want to create a good game with AI it's completely possible, just create it with love and taking care of the small details.
